Ebola Outbreak Hits DRC Tourism Workforce, Sites See Sharp Decline in Activity

An outbreak of Ebola has struck the workforce at several key tourism sites in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, leading to temporary closures and a significant drop in visitor numbers. The situation, which began to unfold last month at Virunga National Park and has since affected multiple other attractions, is ongoing and continues to disrupt operations across the industry.

According to the Congolese Tourism Federation, at least 40 rangers and guides have tested positive for the Ebola virus since the outbreak was first reported. Many have been placed in isolation, and some are receiving treatment in facilities managed by the industry itself. Tour operators including Kivu Adventures and Congo EcoTours have suspended guided activities, while management at Virunga National Park confirmed that all overnight lodges and visitor centers have been closed as a precautionary measure.

“The safety of our staff and guests remains our top priority,” said Jean-Marc Bukasa, spokesperson for the Congolese Tourism Federation. “We have reinforced health protocols at all open sites and are working closely with medical teams to monitor the situation.”

Visitor numbers at affected sites have plummeted, with managers at the Okapi Wildlife Reserve reporting a 70% decrease in daily arrivals. Staff shortages have intensified operational challenges, as many tour guides, hospitality workers, and maintenance personnel remain under quarantine. Some sites have opted to close temporarily, while others maintain only essential services to ensure the safety of remaining guests and workers.

Union representatives have expressed concern over the wellbeing of the workforce. “We are urging all tourism employers to provide adequate protective equipment and support for affected employees,” stated Aimée Kabeya, leader of the National Tourism Workers Union. “Many workers are anxious about their health and the uncertain future of their jobs.”

Industry analysts predict that the outbreak will continue to weigh heavily on the sector in the coming weeks. While authorities have not provided an estimate for when normal operations might resume, stakeholders emphasize the need for sustained health interventions and clear communication to ensure the long-term resilience of the country’s tourism industry.
